summary: 有人从小就认不出熟人的脸，还可能误以为别人也一样。调查、家庭研究和识别测试显示，发展性面孔失认有多种表现，患者会用其他线索应对，实验室成绩却未必反映现实困难。
logic: 区分后天与发展性面孔失认
调查补偿办法及可能成因
讨论测试与现实识别的差距

paragraphs.brief: 雅各在一年的余下时间却无视他
sentences: It was Jacob Hodes’s first day at college.
这是Jacob Hodes大学的第一天。
He can still recall spending an enjoyable afternoon being shown around campus by a second-year student named Daniel Byrne, who happened to be from his home town.
他还记得在校园里度过一个愉快的下午一个叫丹尼尔·伯恩的二年级学生正好来自家乡
Jacob then spent the rest of the year ignoring him.
雅各在一年的余下时间却无视他
‘I never saw him again,’ he says.
他说：我再也没有看见他。
‘Well, I’m sure I walked past him plenty of times, but I just didn’t see him.’
"嗯，我敢肯定我走过他很多次，但我只是没有看到他。"
This behaviour wasn’t intentional.
这种行为不是故意的。
Jacob just couldn’t recollect what his fellow student looked like.
雅各无法回忆起同学的样子。
He had had the same trouble all his life.
他一生都遇到同样的麻烦
Friends and relatives would greet him and he would have no idea who they were.
朋友和亲戚会向他问好他不知道他们是谁

paragraphs.brief: 不过，最近研究人员发现了另一种面部失明，即发育偏执，这种失明不是从出生就存在，就是在生命的早期发展。
sentences: It wasn’t until five years ago that it all made sense.
直到五年前，这一切才有意义。
That was when Hodes was diagnosed with prosopagnosia, a condition that means he is unable to recognise faces.
那时霍德斯被诊断出有亲索帕格诺西亚症，这表明他无法辨认面孔。
According to researchers, he is far from alone.
研究人员认为他远非孤单
In fact, the condition is not that uncommon, but until a few years ago only a few dozen cases had ever been described, and all of these had been caused by brain injury.
事实上，情况并不罕见，但直到几年前，只有几十个病例被描述过，所有这些病例都是脑损伤造成的。
Recently, though, researchers identified a second form of face blindness, developmental prosopagnosia, which is either present from birth or develops very early in life.
不过，最近研究人员发现了另一种面部失明，即发育偏执，这种失明不是从出生就存在，就是在生命的早期发展。

paragraphs.brief: 5 月，美国哈佛大学和伦敦大学学院的研究团队公布了对 1,600 人的网络调查结果。据此推测，最多有 2% 的人在一定程度上存在面孔失认。
sentences: In May a team from Harvard University in the US and University College London (UCL) announced the results of a web survey of 1,600 people, suggesting that up to 2 per cent of people have some degree of face blindness.
5 月，美国哈佛大学和伦敦大学学院的研究团队公布了对 1,600 人的网络调查结果。据此推测，最多有 2% 的人在一定程度上存在面孔失认。

Then in August, Martina Gruter and colleagues at the Institute for Human Genetics in Munster, Germany, similarly reported that 2.5 per cent of 700 secondary-school pupils they had tested had trouble recognising faces.
8月，Martina Gruter和德国Munster人类遗传学研究所的同事同样报告说，在700名中学生中，有2.5%的中学生难以认出面孔。
The results of the surveys took everyone by surprise.
调查的结果令人吃惊。

paragraphs.brief: 布拉德·杜肯克联合广播公司的研究员：“Prosopagnosics 几乎总是知道他们有困难认识人，但通常他们不知道其他人有比他们更好的认知技能。”
sentences: It seems that if you have never known what it is to recognise a face, you don’t necessarily know that you are supposed to be able to.
看来如果你从不知道什么是认得面孔你不一定知道自己应该能认出来

Prosopagnosics almost always know that they have trouble recognising people, but they often don’t realise that other people have better recognition skills than they do, says Brad Duchaine, a researcher at UCL.
布拉德·杜肯克联合广播公司的研究员：“Prosopagnosics 几乎总是知道他们有困难认识人，但通常他们不知道其他人有比他们更好的认知技能。”

paragraphs.brief: 尽管存在这些问题，但大多数发展倾向者都拥有能够克服困难的战略，例如，通过认识头发、衣服或个人的说话方式，因此，除非他们看到熟悉的人脱离了背景、有了新的发型或穿了不同的衣服，他们能够认出人。
sentences: Despite these issues, the majority of developmental prosopagnosics possess strategies that allow them to get around their difficulty—for instance, by recognising hair, clothing, or a person’s way of speaking—so, unless they see a familiar person out of context, with a new hairstyle or in different clothes, they can recognise people just fine.
尽管存在这些问题，但大多数发展倾向者都拥有能够克服困难的战略，例如，通过认识头发、衣服或个人的说话方式，因此，除非他们看到熟悉的人脱离了背景、有了新的发型或穿了不同的衣服，他们能够认出人。
Even so, the discovery of developmental prosopagnosia has attracted attention from neuroscientists keen to discover what is different about the brain of face-blind people.
即便如此，发育偏执的发现也吸引了神经科学家的注意，他们热衷于发现面盲人大脑的不同之处。
This difference, they believe, could help solve the problem of how the brain deals with information in general, not just visual data.
他们认为，这种差异可以帮助解决大脑如何处理一般信息，而不仅仅是视觉数据的问题。
In other words, it may show whether the brain has specialised parts for specific tasks or is more of a general-purpose information processor.
换句话说，它可能表明大脑是具有特定任务的专门部件，还是更具有一般用途的信息处理器。

paragraphs.brief: 也有些人甚至无法在镜子中认出自己的面孔。
sentences: One issue, however, that will present challenges for researchers is that no two prosopagnosics are the same.
然而，对研究人员来说，一个挑战是，没有两种代谢疗法是相同的。
Some have problems only with faces, while others have trouble with ordinary everyday objects and, so it turns out, animals which would normally be familiar as well.
一些人只对面孔有问题，而另一些人则对普通日常物品有问题，结果发现，通常也会熟悉的动物也有问题。
Some prosopagnosics can train themselves to recognise specific faces; others can’t even recognise their own in a mirror.
也有些人甚至无法在镜子中认出自己的面孔。
When some have been tested they could identify the emotion that was conveyed on another’s face, even though the face itself seemed unfamiliar, while for other subjects this was an impossibility.
当有些人经过测试后，他们可以辨别在他人脸上所传达的情感，尽管脸本身似乎不熟悉，而对其他主体来说，这是不可能的。
Some cannot recognise the faces of old friends or fellow students but have no trouble telling whether a particular face from such groups would be attractive to most people.
有些人无法认出老朋友或同学的面孔，但认为这类团体的某一面孔对大多数人是否具有吸引力并不难。
Because of this diversity, working out the cause of prosopagnosia will not be easy.
由于这种多样性，解决无亲无故症的事业并非易事。

paragraphs.brief: 在Martina Gruter的研究中，同意让父母和亲属接受检查的亲生者报告至少有一名有病的亲属。
sentences: In Martina Gruter’s study, the prosopagnosics who agreed to have their parents and relatives tested reported at least one relative with the condition.
在Martina Gruter的研究中，同意让父母和亲属接受检查的亲生者报告至少有一名有病的亲属。
Having looked at 38 cases in seven families, the German team believe they have good evidence that a single gene could be responsible.
德国调查组在调查了7个家庭38个病例后，认为他们有确凿证据表明，一个基因可能要负责。
Duchaine also has some evidence that face blindness could be inherited but thinks other factors might be more significant.
达肯也有一些证据表明，面部失明是可以继承的，但认为其他因素可能更为重要。

He refers to studies of babies born with a condition which means the eye’s lens is not clear, and when it’s the left one, being unable to see through this eye during the first two months of life is a major risk factor for prosopagnosia.
他提到对出生婴儿的研究，这种研究意味着眼睛的透镜不清楚，而当眼睛是左眼时，在生命的头两个月内无法看穿眼睛，这是对亲索帕格诺西亚人的一个主要危险因素。

paragraphs.brief: 不管原因是什么多数的哲学家都想知道他们是否能做点什么来提高他们的面部识别能力
sentences: Whatever the cause, what most prosopagnosics want to know is whether they can do anything to improve their face-recognition skills.
不管原因是什么多数的哲学家都想知道他们是否能做点什么来提高他们的面部识别能力

Joseph DeGutis, a graduate student at the University of California, recently reported successfully training a severe developmental prosopagnosic to recognise faces during tests carried out in the laboratory.
加利福尼亚大学研究生Joseph DeGutis最近报告说，在实验室进行的测试中，成功培训了严格的发育前科，以辨别面孔。
The subject also reported that recognising faces in everyday life became easier due to the training.
该主题还报告说，由于培训，在日常生活中识别面孔变得更加容易。
Duchaine now plans to attempt to train sufferers to recognise the five people they most need to know—maybe their immediate family, for example, and essential colleagues.
杜肯现在计划试图培训受难者，使他们认识他们最需要认识的五个人，例如，可能是他们的直系亲属和必要的同事。
Thomas Gruter, Martina Gruter’s husband, who also works on her team, however, is not convinced it will work.
Thomas Gruter，Martina Gruter的丈夫，也是她的团队工作，但是，他不相信这行得通。
‘I don’t know how you can have more training than you have already had,’ he says.
他说：“我不知道你怎么可以得到更多的训练比你已经有过。”
‘Humans already spend all day looking at faces.’
人已整天看着人的脸。
He also points out that cheating is a possibility during tests and provides an example.
他还指出，在试验期间作弊是一种可能性，并举了一个例子。
One person we studied said that when she was doing the face-recognition test, she memorised the distance between nose and upper lip.
我们研究的一个人说当她做面部识别测试时她记得鼻子和上唇之间的距离
She wasn’t the only one.
她不是唯一的一个。
So you can perform well in the test and not do so well in real life.
这样你就能在测试中表现好而在现实生活中表现不好

items.en: Before attending college, Jacob was capable of recognising people he knew well.
items.zh: 雅各布在上大学之前能够认出他认识的人
items.why: 题干说“能认出”,原文说“一直不行”,直接矛盾，故 False。

items.en: Researchers believe that prosopagnosia may be a growing problem.
items.zh: 研究人员认为，亲索帕格诺西亚可能是一个日益严重的问题。
items.why: 调查估算了当时具有一定脸盲症状的人口比例，没有跨时段数据说明患者是否越来越多。

items.en: It is harder to identify developmental prosopagnosia in babies than in young children.
items.zh: 与幼儿相比，发现婴儿发育偏好更难。
items.why: P2 只说“present from birth or develops very early (出生即有或很早出现)”,未比较“婴儿 vs. 幼儿?的识别难度,NG。

items.en: A German study seems to support the Harvard and UCL research findings.
items.zh: 德国的一项研究似乎支持哈佛大学和大学联合研究的结果。
items.why: “similarly reported (同样报告)” 与相近的比例共同表明两项研究相互印证，故 True.

items.en: In general, prosopagnosics are aware that other people can recognise faces more easily than they can.
items.zh: 一般来说，亲索帕尼诺西克人知道其他人比他们更容易认出面孔
items.why: 题干说“意识到”,原文说“往往没有意识到”,与之相反,False。

items.en: In most cases, prosopagnosics have developed ways to deal with their problem.
items.zh: 在多数情况下，代索帕尼诺西奇人已经制定了解决他们问题的方法。
items.why: “the majority…possess strategies”=“大多数有办法”,与题干一致,True。

items.en: The study of prosopagnosia may help neuroscientists to treat different kinds of brain injury.
items.zh: 研究蛋白质会帮助神经科学家治疗各种脑损伤。
items.why: 原文谈的是理解/机制，未提治疗脑损伤”。故无法推出,NG。

items.zh: 脸盲者可能难以辨认日常常见的________和物品。
items.why: 空格前已有“commonly seen…and objects”, 与原文并列“objects and…animals” 对应。名词复数“animals”符合单词数要求。

items.zh: 他们也可能辨认不出别人脸上流露的________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“当有些人经过测试后，他们可以辨别在他人脸上所传达的情感，尽管脸本身似乎不熟悉，而对其他主体来说，这是不可能的”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: just one ________, according to Martina Gruter
items.zh: 玛蒂娜·格吕特认为，脸盲可能只与一个________有关。
items.why: 回到对应内容“德国调查组在调查了7个家庭38个病例后，认为他们有确凿证据表明，一个基因可能要负责”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: a defect in the ________ eye, according to Brad Duchaine
items.zh: 布拉德·迪谢纳认为，脸盲可能与________眼的缺陷有关。
items.why: 回到对应内容“他提到对出生婴儿的研究，这种研究意味着眼睛的透镜不清楚，而当眼睛是左眼时，在生命的头两个月内无法看穿眼睛，这是对亲索帕格诺西亚人的一个主要危险因素”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Treatment for prosopagnosia Joseph DeGutis’s patient proved he had been successfully trained to recognise faces inside the ________ and in the outside world.
items.zh: 约瑟夫·德古蒂斯的患者证明，训练取得了成效。他不仅能在________里认出人脸，在日常生活中也能做到。
items.why: 空格处应与“outside world” 形成对照，原文唯一对应场域是 laboratory。

items.en: Thomas Gruter doubts that the training will work and mentions that ________ by some subjects can affect research results.
items.zh: 托马斯·格吕特怀疑这种训练能否奏效。他指出，部分受试者的________行为会影响研究结果。
items.why: Thomas Gruter 的质疑具体指“cheating”,与题干完全对应。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 第 5 段 · 第 4 句
第 5 段 · 第 3 句
points: 调查估算了当时具有一定脸盲症状的人口比例，没有跨时段数据说明患者是否越来越多。
空格前已有“commonly seen…and objects”, 与原文并列“objects and…animals” 对应。名词复数“animals”符合单词数要求。
clauses: In May a team from Harvard University in the US and University College London (UCL) announced the results of a web survey of 1,600 people, suggesting ….
“that up to 2 per cent of people have some degree of face blindness”补足 suggesting 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 suggesting 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
It seems that …, you don’t necessarily know that you are supposed to be able to.
连接词 if 引出“if you have never known what it is to recognise a face”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Prosopagnosia is a medical condition that stops people from recognizing people’s faces, but how common is it and why does it happen?
普罗索帕格诺西亚是一种医疗状况，它阻止人们认出人们的面孔，但它有多常见，为什么会发生呢？
